title: Constant prediction baselines
goals: Fit mean and median constant baselines on training targets
Compare constant predictions on separate records
Keep fitted constants independent of evaluation answers

prerequisite.prompt: Why can signed residuals hide error size?
prerequisite.answer: Opposite signs can cancel; a magnitude-based loss avoids that cancellation.

vocabulary: One fixed prediction for every query
Sum of training targets divided by their count
Middle value of sorted training targets

blocks.text: Before a complex regression model, fit a simple constant predictor. A mean baseline uses the training average. A median baseline uses the middle training target. They ignore features but provide a comparison that is easy to reproduce. Evaluation targets must not determine the constants.

Use fictional classroom data throughout this investigation. Keep the task, units, reference labels and data split visible as you reason. Earlier weeks supplied the model-building process; this week examines constant prediction baselines.

Training targets [2, 4, 6, 12] have mean 24/4=6 and median (4+6)/2=5. On separate targets [4, 8], the mean baseline predicts [6, 6] with absolute errors [2, 2], averaging 2. The median baseline predicts [5, 5] with errors [1, 3], also averaging 2.

blocks.title: Python 3 check
blocks.text:
from statistics import mean, median
training = [2, 4, 6, 12]
validation = [4, 8]
for name, value in [("mean", mean(training)),
                    ("median", median(training))]:
    mae = mean(abs(y - value) for y in validation)
    print(name, value, mae)
# Both validation MAEs are 2; constants differ.

Trace the calculation on paper before running this optional Python check. Use the stated fictional inputs and compare intermediate values. The code checks this example; your independent workbook case uses different evidence.

blocks.title: Constant prediction baselines at a glance
blocks.caption: Mean and median answer different training objectives. A mean minimizes total squared error among constants; a median minimizes total absolute error. This does not guarantee either wins on a new evaluation set. With extreme values, the mean can move much more than the median.

blocks.label: Calculate MAE for both baselines on [4, 8]. Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

blocks.text: Replacing training 12 by 40 gives mean 13 and median 5. That change is a data change to record and investigate, not an instruction to delete an inconvenient observation. Decide whether the extreme value is valid using the measurement policy and provenance.

For an even number of values, this course averages the two middle values to report one median. Keep a frozen baseline across comparisons and show its evaluation score. A model that fails to beat it may still reveal a data or metric issue worth investigating.

blocks.label: Why not predict the evaluation mean as the baseline?

workbook.title: Fit two constants
workbook.prompt: Find the mean and median of the worked training targets.

workbook.title: Score separately
workbook.prompt: Calculate MAE for both baselines on [4, 8].
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Both score 2; their per-record absolute errors differ.

workbook.title: Inspect an extreme value
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Mean becomes 13; median stays 5. Investigate validity before deciding treatment.

workbook.title: Apply independently
workbook.prompt: Training [1, 3, 5, 15], evaluation [3, 9]. Fit both constants and calculate MAE.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Mean 6 and median 4. Mean errors [3, 3] MAE 3; median errors [1, 5] MAE 3.

workbook.title: Prevent leakage
workbook.prompt: Why not predict the evaluation mean as the baseline?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: It fits using evaluation answers and makes the baseline unavailable for genuinely unseen cases.

teacher.background: Teach two 45-minute sessions. This week focuses on constant prediction baselines. Model the worked example first, collect the new W 4 case independently before feedback, and use the fresh retry to check transfer. Award credit for traceable reasoning and bounded claims, including justified uncertainty.
materials: Paper, pencils and a calculator for fractions
The fictional examples and a blank evidence table
Optional Python 3 editor; no external packages or AI accounts required
sessions: Use the prerequisite question: Why can signed residuals hide error size? Check the explanation before proceeding.
Read the opening and model the worked evidence. Ask students to identify constant baseline in context.
Complete W 1 and W 2 with support: fit two constants; score separately. Require the evidence, not only the final response.
Read the visual row by row. Collect the guided explanation and compare reasoning in pairs. Trace the Python check after the paper calculation.
Retrieve the distinction between constant baseline and training mean. Invite a counterexample to an overconfident claim.
Discuss the application and complete W 3: Replace 12 by 40. What changes?

Collect W4 independently before giving hints. Assess these outcomes: Fit mean and median constant baselines on training targets; Compare constant predictions on separate records. Record any support used.
Use W 5 and the exit response to assess limits. Give targeted feedback, then the fresh retry. Save evidence of independent understanding.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided response: Both score 2; their per-record absolute errors differ. Exit response: It fits using evaluation answers and makes the baseline unavailable for genuinely unseen cases.
misconceptions: Ask for the relevant counts, units, procedure or saved record. For this week: Mean 6; median 5.

teacher.assessment: For independent W 4, require: Mean 6 and median 4. Mean errors [3, 3] MAE 3; median errors [1, 5] MAE 3. Fresh retry training [2, 2, 8], evaluation [1, 7]: mean 4 median 2; MAE 3 for each. Require training-only fitting. Mark each criterion as independent, supported or not yet demonstrated. Reassess the reasoning after feedback; do not replace the first attempt silently.
teacher.support: Provide a blank evidence table and allow a verbal explanation before writing. Highlight the given conditions without supplying the W 4 conclusion. Use constant baseline and training mean in full sentences. Extension: alter one condition in the worked example and explain which conclusion changes and which remains supported.
